confidence.overallReason: Fresh automated and connected gates pass, but the implementation violates required ownership and bounded-input/cancellation contracts. PhotoAdviceCall finally deletes any File supplied by its caller rather than proving it is an owned transient cache file; unknown-length content URIs bypass the 64 MiB source cap; JSON and multipart context are unbounded; one PhotoAdviceCall can execute concurrently and create two requests; and Firebase Tasks.await has no timeout. Existing green evidence does not exercise these failures and mislabels a whole multipart-body hash/size as JPEG evidence.

task: T5 Android auth/API client and ephemeral photo lifecycle
commitSubject: feat(network): connect secure AI and photo transport

findings.title: Upload cleanup can delete caller-owned or foreign files
findings.requirement: Only owned cache deletion in finally on all paths.
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/LeftoversApi.kt:51-70 accepts an arbitrary java.io.File and carries no PhotoLifecycle ownership proof.

android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/LeftoversApi.kt:111-130 unconditionally calls photo.delete() in finally on success, HTTP error, auth failure, cancellation, malformed file, and oversize file paths.

The fresh passing JVM test error_response_deletes_transient_upload dynamically creates File.createTempFile without the owned cache directory and asserts that this foreign temp file is deleted, locking in the unsafe behavior rather than rejecting it.
findings.impact: A future caller that passes a persistent app file, camera original outside the owned transient directory, or any other caller-controlled File loses it even before a request is created (for example AuthUnavailable or PayloadTooLarge).
findings.requiredFix: Make the upload type/constructor accept only a PhotoLifecycle-created owned artifact, or validate canonical containment in the dedicated leftovers-photos directory before deletion; reject foreign files and add a regression test proving they survive every terminal path.

findings.title: Unknown-length content URIs bypass the source byte limit
findings.requirement: Bound photo input before processing and enforce the source/multipart limits.
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/photo/PhotoLifecycle.kt:77-80 returns AssetFileDescriptor.length directly; Android providers may report UNKNOWN_LENGTH (-1).

android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/photo/PhotoLifecycle.kt:39-48 rejects only length == 0 or length > 64 MiB, so -1 is accepted and decoded from the provider stream without a counting cap.
The oversize test uses RandomAccessFile with a known positive length and does not cover an unknown-length ContentProvider stream.
findings.impact: A picker provider can stream an arbitrarily large or compressed-bomb payload past the intended 64 MiB trust-boundary check, causing excessive I/O or memory/CPU pressure.
findings.requiredFix: Treat negative/unknown length as requiring a bounded copy/counting stream into an owned file, abort at MAX_SOURCE_BYTES + 1, then decode only the bounded artifact.

findings.title: One photo call can create multiple concurrent uploads
findings.requirement: Cancellation exactly one call/no reupload, including repeated interruptions.
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/LeftoversApi.kt:111-127 has no one-shot/atomic executed state.
Two threads can both pass photo.isFile/cancelled, invoke requestFactory, overwrite the shared call field, and execute separate OkHttp calls before either finally deletes the file.
cancel() at lines 133-136 can cancel only whichever call most recently won the shared assignment.
Fresh tests cover one execute thread and two consecutive test runs, not concurrent/repeated execute on the same PhotoAdviceCall.
findings.impact: Duplicate photo uploads and quota/cost consumption are possible; cancellation can leave one in-flight request running.
findings.requiredFix: Use an atomic one-shot state that permits exactly one execute transition and tracks/cancels that single call; add a two-thread regression proving requestCount remains one.

findings.title: JSON and multipart context inputs have no client-side bounds
findings.requirement: Enforce JSON/multipart limits and produce typed boundary failures without unnecessary upload.
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/LeftoversApi.kt:40-48 converts any String to a request body without the 256 KiB JSON limit used by the service contract.
android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/LeftoversApi.kt:51-64 adds contextJson to multipart without a bound; only photo.length is checked later at line 114.
The connected assertion allows multipart body size up to MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 4096 for its tiny context but does not test oversized context.
findings.impact: The client can allocate and transmit requests that the backend must reject as 413, and multipart total size is not bounded by the intended contract.
findings.requiredFix: Apply the canonical UTF-8 JSON/context byte cap before token acquisition/request construction and return PayloadTooLarge with requestCount zero.

findings.title: Firebase token acquisition can hang indefinitely
findings.requirement: Hung operations must terminate with a typed result/cancellable boundary.
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/network/AnonymousFirebaseTokenProvider.kt:14-16 uses both Tasks.await calls without a timeout.
PhotoAdviceCall cancellation cannot interrupt tokenProvider.idToken because the OkHttp Call does not exist until token acquisition completes.
No AnonymousFirebaseTokenProvider test simulates a never-completing sign-in/token task.
findings.impact: Network/auth degradation can strand the worker indefinitely and make cancel appear ineffective until Firebase eventually completes.
findings.requiredFix: Use a bounded token wait or a cancellable async provider and map timeout/cancellation to AuthUnavailable/Cancelled.

findings.title: Committed lifecycle evidence overstates what was observed
evidence: PhotoPickerTest reads request.body.readByteArray(), then writes body.size and sha256(body) under fields named jpegBytes and sha256. Those values describe the entire multipart body including its randomized boundary, not the JPEG part.
The committed multipart hash 490f88bc... differs from the fresh run hash 1ee07fe0... while image dimensions/fixture are unchanged, consistent with hashing the randomized multipart envelope.

task-5-green.txt accurately calls restart simulated, but task-5-cancel.txt exposes restart_entrypoint while the test constructs a second Application and calls onCreate in the same process; no real process restart is executed.
findings.impact: The artifact cannot independently prove exact JPEG bytes or a real process-restart lifecycle even though its field names and summary can be read that way.
findings.requiredFix: Parse the recorded multipart and hash/assert the photo part itself; name total multipart bytes separately. Either run an actual force-stop/relaunch sweep or label the evidence strictly as direct onCreate invocation.

findings.title: EXIF transpose and transverse orientations are ignored
evidence: android/app/src/main/java/com/junited31/leftovers/photo/PhotoLifecycle.kt:102-110 handles rotate 90/180/270 and horizontal/vertical flip but not ORIENTATION_TRANSPOSE or ORIENTATION_TRANSVERSE.
The sole EXIF regression covers only ORIENTATION_ROTATE_90.
findings.impact: JPEGs using EXIF orientations 5 or 7 are uploaded with incorrect visual orientation.
findings.requiredFix: Handle all eight EXIF orientation values and add one mirrored-rotation regression.

authBoundary.evidence: AnonymousFirebaseTokenProvider uses FirebaseAuth anonymous sign-in/current-user ID token and no production secret or conditional test bypass was found. TokenProvider injection is used by tests, not selected by a runtime test flag. Live Firebase configuration is absent and is deferred to the later deployment task; this review does not claim a live token was minted.

typedHttpAndNoRetry.evidence: OkHttp is forced to retryOnConnectionFailure(false) even for an injected client; fresh tests map 200/401/413/422/429/502, network disconnect, and cancellation. Token wait remains unbounded as a separate finding.

photoTransform.evidence: Fresh real-device test generated a 2600x1800 MediaStore JPEG, passed it through PickVisualMedia.parseResult, compressed to 1280x886 JPEG at quality 80, sent one recorded request, and observed the owned cache empty. Known-length size enforcement and rotate-90 EXIF pass; unknown-length and EXIF 5/7 remain gaps.

nativeContracts.evidence: Connected PhotoPickerTest used PickVisualMedia.ImageOnly parsing and verified TakePicture EXTRA_OUTPUT equals an app FileProvider content URI. No CameraX dependency/source was found.

startupSweep.evidence: LeftoversApplication.onCreate invokes sweepStale. JVM coverage deletes only files under cacheDir/leftovers-photos older than 24h and preserves a 23h owned file plus a 7-day file outside that directory. Connected direct onCreate invocation deletes a 25h owned fixture.

FileProvider is non-exported, grants URI permissions, and exposes only cache-path leftovers-photos/ rather than the cache root/files/external root.
